name: Cherubism
aliases: Familial fibrous dysplasia of the jaws
Familial multilocular cystic disease of the jaws

criteria.description: Bilateral painless swelling of the mandible and/or maxilla
Multilocular radiolucent lesions in the jaw bones on imaging
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Identification of pathogenic SH3BP2 gene mutation
Fibro-osseous tissue with multinucleated giant cells on biopsy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of bilateral jaw swelling with characteristic radiographic lesions; genetic testing or family history supportive but not mandatory
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and radiographic; genetic confirmation supports diagnosis

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bilateral painless mandibular and maxillary swelling
searchTerms: swelling on both sides of jaw
painless lumps in upper and lower jaw
multiple cyst-like areas in jaw bone
jaw bone with several hollow spots
multichambered dark areas on jaw x-ray
full round face with chubby cheeks
plump facial appearance like a cherub
late coming in of adult teeth

occasional.symptomName: Visual disturbances due to orbital involvement
searchTerms: vision problems from eye socket issues
eye disturbances due to orbital involvement
blurred or double vision from eye area

occasional.symptomName: Pain or tenderness in jaw region

searchTerms: jaw bone breaks from minor injury

rare.symptomName: Hearing loss secondary to Eustachian tube dysfunction
searchTerms: hearing loss due to ear tube problems
impaired hearing from Eustachian tube dysfunction

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; no specific laboratory abnormalities
imaging: Panoramic radiographs showing bilateral multilocular radiolucent lesions of the jaws
CT scan demonstrating expansile fibro-osseous lesions with cortical thinning
genetic: Mutations in SH3BP2 gene on chromosome 4p16.3
other: Histopathology revealing fibrous stroma with multinucleated giant cells

distinguishingFeatures: Different radiographic appearance with ground-glass opacity

references: Marck KW, et al. Cherubism: clinical and molecular findings. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2014.
Ueki Y. Cherubism: a genetic perspective. Oral Dis. 2015.
American Academy of Oral and Maxillofacial Radiology. Cherubism imaging features. 2020.
